project.title: Rentemester Rust migration — reviewed delivery plan
project.goal: One accounting engine for server/web, remote native desktop and fully local native desktop.
project.scope: Complete issue decomposition and dependencies; implementation readiness is evaluated per refined slice, not claimed by this graph.
assumptions: Rust backend/CLI/MCP and GPUI desktop are proposed; retain React web.
One deployment per customer organization; separate legal-entity ledgers.
SQLite retained subject to explicit compatibility verification.
A managed local HTTP runtime shares the server API.
All nodes are sketches; scenarios are planned, not executed.

boundary.rationale: Keep accounting semantics reusable across every client.

component.application.label: Application
component.application.description: Use cases, company permissions, policy and atomic write orchestration.

boundary.responsibility: Use cases, company permissions, policy and atomic write orchestration.
boundary.rationale: All interfaces must enforce the same business gates.

component.storage.label: Storage
component.storage.description: SQLite, migrations, audit/evidence persistence and verified workspace transfer.

boundary.responsibility: SQLite, migrations, audit/evidence persistence and verified workspace transfer.
boundary.rationale: Preserve durable company data behind one owning runtime.
excludes: Business authorization and direct UI access

component.integrations.label: Integrations
component.integrations.description: External provider protocols and durable effect delivery.

boundary.responsibility: External provider protocols and durable effect delivery.
boundary.rationale: Provider outages and retries need independent reconciliation.

component.runtime.label: Runtime
component.runtime.description: HTTP API, authentication translation, discovery and process lifecycle.

boundary.responsibility: HTTP API, authentication translation, discovery and process lifecycle.
boundary.rationale: Local and hosted clients share one server contract.

component.agent.label: Agent
component.agent.description: Local/remote CLI and MCP with explicit context and structured errors.

boundary.responsibility: Local/remote CLI and MCP with explicit context and structured errors.
boundary.rationale: Agent tools need stable discoverable preconditions and effects.

component.desktop.label: Desktop
component.desktop.description: GPUI views, connection profiles and a managed local backend.

boundary.responsibility: GPUI views, connection profiles and a managed local backend.
boundary.rationale: A native experience must support local and remote operation.
excludes: SQL access, ledger rules and offline replay

component.web.label: Web
component.web.description: React browser views and same-origin API interaction.

boundary.responsibility: React browser views and same-origin API interaction.
boundary.rationale: Retain existing browser investment and separate rendering from accounting.
excludes: SQL access and local process management

entity.ledger.label: Ledger
entity.ledger.description: A separate ledger for each legal entity; immutable booked entries and corrections.

entity.evidence.label: Evidence
entity.evidence.description: Immutable content-addressed original documents with verified references.

entity.workspace.label: Workspace
entity.workspace.description: Organization control state and explicit company membership.

entity.connection.label: Connection
entity.connection.description: Local or remote connection identity; never silently switch after failure.

entity.effect.label: Effect
entity.effect.description: Durable external-delivery intent with unresolved outcomes retained.

action.negotiate.label: Negotiate
action.negotiate.description: Read protocol version/capabilities before opening a workspace.
action.negotiate.behavior: Refuse incompatible operations; negotiation changes no accounting state.

postconditions: Refuse incompatible operations; negotiation changes no accounting state.

action.authenticate.label: Authenticate
action.authenticate.description: Establish trusted local or hosted context.
action.authenticate.behavior: Validate host-owned local credential or configured hosted identity; never trust body actor; exact native identity flow remains open.

postconditions: Validate host-owned local credential or configured hosted identity; never trust body actor; exact native identity flow remains open.

action.validate.label: Validate
action.validate.description: Evaluate exact money, balance, date/currency and policy invariants.
action.validate.behavior: Return all applicable typed refusals with no storage or network effects.

postconditions: Return all applicable typed refusals with no storage or network effects.

action.report.label: Report
action.report.description: Read an authorized company and return an exact trial balance.
action.report.behavior: Authorize company before access; refuse unsupported schemas without migrating; read a consistent snapshot; compute exact totals and deterministic output; do not modify files.

postconditions: Authorize company before access; refuse unsupported schemas without migrating; read a consistent snapshot; compute exact totals and deterministic output; do not modify files.

action.post.label: Post
action.post.description: Post one authorized confirmed journal request with atomic audit and idempotency.
action.post.behavior: Authorize current access; check confirmed payload/revision and policy gates; evaluate domain; use a serialized company transaction to persist journal, audit and key result; retry same key returns original receipt after authorization; rollback on failure.

postconditions: Authorize current access; check confirmed payload/revision and policy gates; evaluate domain; use a serialized company transaction to persist journal, audit and key result; retry same key returns original receipt after authorization; rollback on failure.

action.store.label: Store
action.store.description: Persist one application-approved unit of work.
action.store.behavior: Commit all ledger/audit/idempotency records together or none. File publication uses staging/recovery, not an assumed cross-filesystem transaction.

postconditions: Commit all ledger/audit/idempotency records together or none. File publication uses staging/recovery, not an assumed cross-filesystem transaction.

action.deliver.label: Deliver
action.deliver.description: Deliver an explicitly committed external effect.
action.deliver.behavior: Retry only according to provider capability; retain ambiguous outcomes for reconciliation; never independently book.

postconditions: Retry only according to provider capability; retain ambiguous outcomes for reconciliation; never independently book.

action.connect.label: Connect
action.connect.description: Select local managed runtime or remote server explicitly.
action.connect.behavior: Local: start compatible runtime on authenticated loopback and await readiness. Remote: HTTPS, authenticate and negotiate. Scope caches to server/account/workspace/company; no offline fallback.

postconditions: Local: start compatible runtime on authenticated loopback and await readiness. Remote: HTTPS, authenticate and negotiate. Scope caches to server/account/workspace/company; no offline fallback.

action.web_request.label: Web Request
action.web_request.description: Execute a browser interaction through the same-origin API.
action.web_request.behavior: Keep business decisions on server; display actionable refusals and uncertain writes.

postconditions: Keep business decisions on server; display actionable refusals and uncertain writes.

action.agent_request.label: Agent Request
action.agent_request.description: Execute an explicitly scoped CLI command or MCP tool.
action.agent_request.behavior: Resolve local/remote connection, check protocol and carry trusted identity; preserve structured errors and confirmation requirements.

postconditions: Resolve local/remote connection, check protocol and carry trusted identity; preserve structured errors and confirmation requirements.

action.migrate.label: Migrate
action.migrate.description: Verify and publish an explicit workspace move or cutover.
action.migrate.behavior: Fence old writer; verify staged snapshot, audit and evidence; re-provision destination identity; activate one writer. Reject corruption and unsupported formats; no silent synchronization.

postconditions: Fence old writer; verify staged snapshot, audit and evidence; re-provision destination identity; activate one writer. Reject corruption and unsupported formats; no silent synchronization.

rule.shared_engine.label: Shared Engine
rule.shared_engine.description: Every client executes accounting operations through the same application/domain contracts; clients cannot mutate SQL directly.

rule.statement: Every client executes accounting operations through the same application/domain contracts; clients cannot mutate SQL directly.

rule.company_isolation.label: Company Isolation
rule.company_isolation.description: Authorize the explicit company before accessing its ledger or evidence; company-specific names, mappings and values remain workspace data.

rule.statement: Authorize the explicit company before accessing its ledger or evidence; company-specific names, mappings and values remain workspace data.

rule.exact_money.label: Exact Money
rule.exact_money.description: Amounts and rates have explicit scale/rounding and checked arithmetic; wire money is exact strings, never authoritative JSON floats.

rule.statement: Amounts and rates have explicit scale/rounding and checked arithmetic; wire money is exact strings, never authoritative JSON floats.

rule.atomic_posting.label: Atomic Posting
rule.atomic_posting.description: Journal, audit and idempotency result commit atomically; reversal appends new records; errors leave no partial journal.

rule.statement: Journal, audit and idempotency result commit atomically; reversal appends new records; errors leave no partial journal.

rule.single_writer.label: Single Writer
rule.single_writer.description: One runtime owns each writable workspace; no TypeScript/Rust dual writes, multi-master or remote-offline replay.

rule.statement: One runtime owns each writable workspace; no TypeScript/Rust dual writes, multi-master or remote-offline replay.

rule.profile_security.label: Profile Security
rule.profile_security.description: Remote access requires hosted authentication and HTTPS; local mode uses private authenticated loopback and never falls back from remote failure.

rule.statement: Remote access requires hosted authentication and HTTPS; local mode uses private authenticated loopback and never falls back from remote failure.

rule.compatibility.label: Compatibility
rule.compatibility.description: Preserve verified ledger/evidence/audit and security semantics or make a diagnosed change explicit; no silent downgrade or incompatible rollback.

rule.statement: Preserve verified ledger/evidence/audit and security semantics or make a diagnosed change explicit; no silent downgrade or incompatible rollback.

scenario.local.label: Local
scenario.local.description: A managed compatible backend is ready; local reports work without internet.

scenario.given: A user selects a local workspace.
scenario.when: Open desktop.
scenario.then: A managed compatible backend is ready; local reports work without internet.

scenario.remote.label: Remote
scenario.remote.description: It reads the same authoritative report as the web client.

scenario.given: An authenticated account has company membership.
scenario.when: Connect native desktop to its HTTPS server.
scenario.then: It reads the same authoritative report as the web client.

scenario.isolation.label: Isolation
scenario.isolation.description: Deny access before company data is opened; leak no evidence.

scenario.given: A user lacks membership in another company.
scenario.when: Request that company report or evidence.
scenario.then: Deny access before company data is opened; leak no evidence.

scenario.exact.label: Exact
scenario.exact.description: Match fixed independent expectations and legacy results or explain diagnosed defects; reject overflow.

scenario.given: Synthetic journals include negative, fractional and numeric-boundary values.
scenario.when: Compute a trial balance.
scenario.then: Match fixed independent expectations and legacy results or explain diagnosed defects; reject overflow.

scenario.readonly.label: Readonly
scenario.readonly.description: Ledger and evidence byte hashes remain unchanged; no schema migration occurs.

scenario.given: A supported copied ledger is hashed before opening.
scenario.when: Read a trial balance.
scenario.then: Ledger and evidence byte hashes remain unchanged; no schema migration occurs.

scenario.schema.label: Schema
scenario.schema.description: Refuse clearly and leave all bytes unchanged.

scenario.given: The copied ledger has an unsupported schema.
scenario.when: Open it read-only.
scenario.then: Refuse clearly and leave all bytes unchanged.

scenario.unbalanced.label: Unbalanced
scenario.unbalanced.description: Reject with no journal/audit/idempotency success residue.

scenario.given: An authorized confirmed request has unequal debits and credits.
scenario.when: Attempt posting.
scenario.then: Reject with no journal/audit/idempotency success residue.

scenario.retry.label: Retry
scenario.retry.description: One journal and original receipt; changed payload with same key conflicts.

scenario.given: Two identical authorized requests share a scoped key.
scenario.when: Submit concurrently and retry after a lost response.
scenario.then: One journal and original receipt; changed payload with same key conflicts.

scenario.crash.label: Crash
scenario.crash.description: No partial journal, audit success or idempotency success remains.

scenario.given: Persistence fails before commit.
scenario.when: Interrupt posting.
scenario.then: No partial journal, audit success or idempotency success remains.

scenario.disconnected.label: Disconnected
scenario.disconnected.description: Show uncertainty and reconcile original key; never create an automatic local write.

scenario.given: A remote write response is lost.
scenario.when: Reconnect or switch profile.
scenario.then: Show uncertainty and reconcile original key; never create an automatic local write.

scenario.revoke.label: Revoke
scenario.revoke.description: Only authorized sequential outcomes occur; exact ordering is unresolved and blocks hosted implementation.

scenario.given: A company membership is being revoked while a write is attempted.
scenario.when: Interleave revocation and posting under the future explicit serialization contract.
scenario.then: Only authorized sequential outcomes occur; exact ordering is unresolved and blocks hosted implementation.

scenario.move.label: Move
scenario.move.description: Refuse activation, preserve source, and never enable a second writer.

scenario.given: A staged snapshot contains altered evidence or unsupported schema.
scenario.when: Attempt activation.
scenario.then: Refuse activation, preserve source, and never enable a second writer.

scenario.expired.label: Expired
scenario.expired.description: Deny access and clear client visibility/caches for that session.

scenario.given: A hosted session has been revoked.
scenario.when: Attempt access from web or desktop.
scenario.then: Deny access and clear client visibility/caches for that session.

scenario.effect.label: Effect
scenario.effect.description: Keep outcome unresolved until safe reconciliation; do not claim exactly-once delivery.

scenario.given: A provider times out after possibly delivering an effect.
scenario.when: Recover the durable task.
scenario.then: Keep outcome unresolved until safe reconciliation; do not claim exactly-once delivery.

community.delivery.p1.description: Rust foundation and first read-only vertical slice

action.delivery.r01.label: R01 Freeze the migration baseline and complete the feature/contract inventory
action.delivery.r01.description: Define exactly what must survive the rewrite before treating module counts or passing tests as coverage.
action.delivery.r01.behavior:
Inventory core operations, schema/migrations, HTTP routes, CLI keys, MCP tools, browser screens, providers, jobs and release contracts
Record supported, partial, unavailable and open-roadmap status at an exact working-tree revision
Map every behavior to one delivery issue, oracle, negative case and applicable interface; rebase the inventory at each cutover candidate
Record per-operation input, success/refusal/parse/protocol failure schemas, casing, nullability, stdout/stderr/exit behavior, MCP text/structuredContent and CLI-only/MCP-only boundaries.

postconditions: No unowned product capability, route, command or screen remains; intentional exclusions name an existing issue and reason
Open enhancements are not silently declared implemented or imported as new rewrite scope
Record existing known bugs separately from behavior to preserve; changes in the old product trigger an explicit delta review

action.delivery.r02.label: R02 Specify GDD contracts, component boundaries and per-slice readiness
action.delivery.r02.description: Refine the target graph into executable work scopes without equating valid plans with implementation evidence.
action.delivery.r02.behavior:
Retain stable IDs, preserved source bytes and revision-bound model change records
Define public application/domain/storage contracts and precise forbidden imports
Define a readiness checklist and independent acceptance/check plans for each slice

postconditions: Each implementation scope has typed inputs/context/output, effects, errors, postconditions and five risk categories with scenarios
Model validity, authorization, readiness and execution evidence remain separate
A source-based architecture negative control detects a forbidden client-to-storage import; planned labels alone cannot pass it

action.delivery.r03.label: R03 Define exact money, schema, audit and wire compatibility
action.delivery.r03.description: Resolve numeric and persistent-format compatibility before selecting Rust representations or enabling readers/writers.
action.delivery.r03.behavior:
Document supported SQLite/control-schema versions, triggers, constraints, migration checksums and read-only snapshot behavior
Define monetary bounds, currency scale, rounding, FX rates, dates, identifiers, JSON encoding and canonical hash/signature bytes
Decide additive/versioned API changes for existing JSON-number clients versus exact-string clients
Specify preservation or explicit mapping of stable principal, workspace/company/ledger identities and idempotency receipts/tombstones across credential rotation, re-enrollment and local/server transfer.

postconditions: Synthetic cross-language vectors cover boundary/overflow, negative/tie rounding, dates, Unicode, null/omitted fields and historical canonicalization
Legacy hashes/signatures validate without rewriting old audit history; incompatible formats fail closed
An explicit compatibility matrix defines schema direction, old-client behavior and rollback constraints
A lost-response mutation retried after credential/host migration cannot execute twice; unsupported identity mapping blocks cutover rather than inventing a new scope.

action.delivery.r04.label: R04 Resolve hosted/native identity and cross-database authorization ordering
action.delivery.r04.description: Choose a supported identity approach and an enforceable revocation/commit ordering before porting authenticated writes.
action.delivery.r04.behavior:
Compare retaining Better Auth during transition with the eventual supported Rust-hosted identity design
Specify browser/native login, MFA/recovery/reset, service principals, credential migration and re-enrollment where required
Define linearization/fencing for membership revocation versus company-ledger commit and process-crash recovery
Specify execution authority and revoke/cancel/lease/dispatch ordering for already committed external jobs, including provider-consent changes, crash and restore.

postconditions: A decision record selects implementable identity and synchronization contracts with threat model, revocation ordering and failure semantics
Existing MFA/recovery/session/last-owner/service-account protections are explicitly preserved
A temporary TypeScript identity dependency has a named removal gate and cannot satisfy the all-Rust-backend exit criterion
Decision tables cover revoke before dispatch, during an external call, after lease expiry and after restore; committed job history does not silently grant permanent future authority.

action.delivery.r05.label: R05 Specify versioned API, typed failures and capability negotiation
action.delivery.r05.description: Give React, GPUI, CLI and MCP one explicit transport contract for compatibility and uncertain writes.
action.delivery.r05.behavior:
Specify OpenAPI/JSON-schema or equivalent versioned request/response contracts, exact amounts and binary/file routes
Define limits, pagination/filter ordering, errors, idempotency/revision/confirm semantics and capabilities
Document auth-required discovery versus public build/protocol metadata and compatibility windows
Produce an operation-by-operation retry matrix: key support/scope/TTL/tombstone, natural dedup, authoritative read-back and unresolved provider outcome; adding key support is an explicit versioned implementation change.
Record exact CLI versus MCP versus HTTP success/error schema mappings; retain existing intentionally distinct envelopes, arrays, field casing and SDK errors through an explicit compatibility policy.

postconditions: Old React clients have an explicit supported compatibility path; no numeric-wire breaking change is silent
Unknown capabilities/incompatible protocol refuse dependent actions before mutation
Lost response, malformed binary error, revoked session and cancelled reads have explicit safe client outcomes
Every advertised operation has an exact input/success/refusal/parse-protocol schema and a retry class; generic original-key recovery is never promised for unsupported operations.

action.delivery.r06.label: R06 Qualify GPUI Kit, accessibility and target-platform feasibility
action.delivery.r06.description: Prove the native toolkit can serve accounting workflows before committing to full desktop implementation.
action.delivery.r06.behavior:
Pin/evaluate GPUI Kit and GPUI licenses/toolchain/platforms using official sources
Prototype virtualized tables, keyboard/focus, accessibility, input/IME, file dialogs and PDF/evidence preview
Assess macOS/Windows/Linux packaging and credential-store integration; preserve current visual identity

postconditions: A small read-only synthetic prototype is exercised on each claimed platform with recorded versions and limitations
Keyboard/screen-reader, large-table and document-preview checks have observable results
Any inability to meet the GPUI product direction is reported as a decision blocker, not silently replaced by another UI stack

action.delivery.r07.label: R07 Bootstrap the Rust workspace, build tooling and architecture checks
action.delivery.r07.description: Add the smallest buildable Rust foundation while preserving the current TypeScript product.
action.delivery.r07.behavior:
Create locked Cargo/toolchain setup and engine/server/client/CLI/MCP/desktop build boundaries as needed
Add lint, formatting, deterministic test entrypoints, license/dependency checks and source-based boundary checks
Keep TypeScript build/release paths working throughout transition

postconditions: Fresh supported development setup builds/tests a minimal engine and binary without hidden machine state
Forbidden UI/network/SQL imports into domain are caught with a negative control
No new production runtime dependencies or needless crate layers are introduced without a consumer

action.delivery.r08.label: R08 Build the synthetic differential and fault-injection acceptance harness
action.delivery.r08.description: Make behavior preservation independently measurable without treating the existing implementation as infallible.
action.delivery.r08.behavior:
Create synthetic multi-company ledgers, documents, migrations and fixed hand-calculated expected outcomes
Execute TypeScript and Rust operations on isolated copies; compare canonical business state, refusals and audit
Support clock/ID determinism, transport loss, process crashes and provider fakes; retain revision-bound receipts

postconditions: Known wrong amount, omitted gate, cross-company access and injected partial commit make the harness fail
Existing defects are recorded with explicit corrected expectations instead of copied blindly
Real company data and credentials are absent; source/oracle files are not mutated by a comparison run

action.delivery.r09.label: R09 Implement exact accounting value types and invariant evaluation
action.delivery.r09.description: Make amounts, currencies, dates and accounting validation explicit Rust domain values.
action.delivery.r09.behavior:
Implement checked exact monetary/rate arithmetic and canonical serialization from R03
Port fiscal dates, account/ID types, debit-credit balance and rule-version evaluation
Return typed refusals with no I/O from pure validation

postconditions: Cross-language boundary/rounding vectors and independent fixed expectations pass
Overflow, invalid currency/scale/date and unbalanced input fail without coercion
Pure domain code has no network, UI, SQL or credential dependency

action.delivery.r10.label: R10 Implement a strictly read-only SQLite/workspace adapter
action.delivery.r10.description: Read supported data without accidental migrations, WAL changes or adoption of unknown directories.
action.delivery.r10.behavior:
Open supported company and control schemas through an explicit read-only snapshot strategy
Resolve workspace/company paths safely and reject symlink/path escape or unsupported schemas
Expose consistent typed read queries and close handles deterministically

postconditions: Before/after workspace byte inventories are unchanged, including WAL/SHM policy specified in R03
Unsupported/future schema, corrupt database, missing ledger and traversal fail closed
Two synthetic companies cannot be confused by slug/path reuse

action.delivery.r11.label: R11 Deliver the first Rust vertical slice: read-only trial-balance parity
action.delivery.r11.description: Demonstrate one complete user outcome through Rust before expanding the rewrite.
action.delivery.r11.behavior:
Read an explicitly selected synthetic company and report its trial balance over a consistent snapshot
Provide a bounded read-only fixture runner and fixed output contract
Compare period, reversal, opening-balance and foreign-currency cases to fixed and legacy expectations

postconditions: Exact totals and deterministic ordering pass for zero, negative, boundary and multi-company fixtures
Unsupported schema/access and invalid periods fail without writes
Source byte-inventory proof and revision-bound comparison output are attached; this slice does not enable live posting

action.delivery.r12.label: R12 Implement workspace ownership, transactional storage and safe migrations
action.delivery.r12.description: Establish one writable runtime and verifiable schema changes before domain mutation work.
action.delivery.r12.behavior:
Implement workspace ownership/IPC discovery, busy handling and verified stale-owner recovery
Port company/control migrations, checksums, append-only guards, sequence allocation and transaction primitives
Define lock ordering, crash/fsync semantics and read/write coexistence; refuse simultaneous legacy/Rust writers

postconditions: Two runtime processes cannot acquire one workspace; PID reuse and stale/missing lock cases do not permit unsafe takeover
Migration failure/crash leaves a recoverable old or fully migrated schema with no half-applied state
Unsupported downgrade, tampered migration and direct UPDATE/DELETE against immutable records fail

action.delivery.r13.label: R13 Port workspace/company authorization and revocation fencing
action.delivery.r13.description: Carry company access and actor attribution into every Rust use case with explicit concurrent revocation semantics.
action.delivery.r13.behavior:
Port membership/RBAC, workspace access/bootstrap/invitations and last-owner invariants
Implement R04 trusted principal and authorization fencing across control and ledger stores
Preserve authorization-denial/audit records without allowing rejected writes to leave business residue

postconditions: Permission matrix and cross-company/file/portfolio tests pass for human, local and service identities
Concurrent revoke/post and last-owner removals produce only the specified allowed sequential outcomes
Caller-supplied actor or workspace ownership alone cannot grant company access

action.delivery.r14.label: R14 Port atomic posting, reversal, idempotency and shared mutation gates
action.delivery.r14.description: Provide the single authoritative write pipeline used by all interfaces.
action.delivery.r14.behavior:
Port dry-run/post/reverse with actor, confirm, period, evidence, backup and rule gates
Commit journal, audit chain, sequences and scoped idempotency receipt together
Preserve expiry/tombstone/replay behavior and exact refusal taxonomy; compose later VAT/domain validators before their features are enabled

postconditions: Crash between every write rolls back all business-success state; reversal appends rather than edits
Concurrent same-key calls return one receipt; changed payload conflicts; revoked replays reveal no protected result
Closed period, missing confirmation, invalid evidence and backup-lock denial leave no partial posting

action.delivery.r15.label: R15 Port immutable document storage, safe ingestion and evidence access
action.delivery.r15.description: Preserve original accounting evidence across filesystem and ledger crashes.
action.delivery.r15.behavior:
Port type/size validation, hashing, deduplication, immutable original registration and access auditing
Stage and verify files before publication; reconcile orphan/staged files after interruption
Preserve document metadata/context/link history and original byte identity

postconditions: Crash at each file/database boundary leaves no committed dangling reference and no silent loss of registered originals
Traversal, symlinks, concurrent replacement, fake file extension and unauthorized document access fail
Duplicate ingest is deterministic and metadata changes never rewrite original evidence

action.delivery.r16.label: R16 Port accounts, contacts, parties and supplier identity
action.delivery.r16.description: Retain reusable master data and evidence-bound business identities without company-specific defaults.
action.delivery.r16.behavior:
Port chart/accounts/roles, contacts/customers/vendors, party registry/assertions and supplier identity
Preserve source-bound document-party links, review and supersession semantics
Keep configuration/mappings local to each workspace and resolve ambiguous identity to review

postconditions: Same supplier name with different legal identities cannot be merged silently
Historical party decisions remain auditable; conflicting review/version input fails
Synthetic company configurations produce distinct valid account mappings; no real CVR/accounts are hardcoded

action.delivery.r17.label: R17 Port VAT rules, purchase evidence, filings and reconciliations
action.delivery.r17.description: Preserve the complete configured Danish VAT behavior and evidence requirements.
action.delivery.r17.behavior:
Port VAT line/account semantics, purchase preflight/evidence, reverse charge, representation and non-VAT cases
Port period reports, return/filing lifecycle, roll-forward, VIES-list and OSS behavior
Retain documented legal-rule versions and explicit legacy corrections

postconditions: Synthetic domestic/EU/foreign/no-VAT and mixed evidence cases match fixed expected amounts and rubric mappings
Missing/ambiguous basis, inconsistent net/VAT/gross and closed filing periods refuse safely
Filed/legacy evidence is never silently reinterpreted; differences from known bugs are explicit

Across API/web/native, VAT tasks show period/basis, blockers/source evidence and next action, and distinguish computed draft, reviewed/locked and actually recorded filing; unsupported automatic submission is stated plainly.

action.delivery.r18.label: R18 Port invoice issuance, immutable PDFs and invoice numbering
action.delivery.r18.description: Issue valid invoices once with immutable evidence and consistent accounting identifiers.
action.delivery.r18.behavior:
Port invoice drafts/validation/issuance, legal fields, currencies, numbering and issued snapshots
Port deterministic PDF generation/rendering and archive verification
Separate creation/rendering from explicit delivery effects

postconditions: Concurrent issue allocates unique scoped numbers and one immutable issued snapshot
Render/read cannot replace an issued PDF; interrupted issue recovers without orphan success
Missing mandatory data and mismatched evidence fail; retry does not issue/send another invoice

action.delivery.r19.label: R19 Port receivables, settlement, credits, FX and overdue claims
action.delivery.r19.description: Carry the entire issued-invoice lifecycle into the shared Rust engine.
action.delivery.r19.behavior:
Port payments/settlement, refunds, credit notes, imported receivables and bad-debt handling
Port FX differences, reminders, interest and compensation with configured rule versions
Maintain exact invoice-to-journal/bank evidence and reversal relationships

postconditions: Partial/full payment, overpayment, credit/refund, FX gain/loss and bad-debt scenarios reconcile to journal/bank
Duplicate settlement/claim and invalid reversal/reference combinations cannot overstate balances
Legacy externally issued receivables are not reissued or resent during migration

action.delivery.r20.label: R20 Port purchases, payables and supplier commitments
action.delivery.r20.description: Preserve expense/payable workflows, documented tax basis and recurring supplier obligations.
action.delivery.r20.behavior:
Port direct expense, payable registration/payment and purchase-VAT evidence
Port supplier-commitment schedules, occurrence matching and corrections
Keep bank-based and payable-based correction paths consistent and auditable

postconditions: Direct-bank purchase and payable paths produce the same intended expense/VAT without duplicate liabilities
Partial payment, corrected tax basis and commitment occurrence replays preserve exact evidence links
Ambiguous/duplicate document identity and unsupported VAT treatment remain review blockers

action.delivery.r21.label: R21 Port canonical bank import, matching and reconciliation corrections
action.delivery.r21.description: Retain one canonical bank truth across CSV and future providers.
action.delivery.r21.behavior:
Port bank accounts/profiles, source identity/import overlap, matching and reconciliation links
Port bank-journal and direct-purchase correction history
Carry resolved contracts from existing identity/reconciliation issues rather than creating parallel fixes

postconditions: Overlapping imports, changed evidence, duplicate rows and multiple observations produce deterministic canonical results
One journal cannot reconcile incompatible/multiple bank transactions contrary to reviewed rules
Correction/replay/rollback cases preserve balances and history with multi-company isolation

action.delivery.r22.label: R22 Port posting rules, exceptions and bank-based bookkeeping workbench
action.delivery.r22.description: Keep the reviewable bank-to-evidence-to-posting workflow coherent across interfaces.
action.delivery.r22.behavior:
Port posting-rule proposal/review/application and exception queues
Port deterministic workbench suggestions, purchase grouping and review evidence
Separate suggestions/dry-runs from confirmed accounting effects
